app.name: Microsoft Outlook (Microsoft Graph via Microsoft Entra ID app registration)

verdict.summary: You can register an Entra app and connect your own mailbox in minutes, and Microsoft has no app-store review for a standard OAuth app. Reaching users in other organisations is the hard part: tenant consent policies and Microsoft's block on unverified multitenant apps mean you will in practice need publisher verification, which depends on a vetted Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account and a verified custom domain.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for the app and Composio config; plus 1-3 hours for publisher verification if you still need a Partner Program account and a custom domain
verdict.approval_wait: No Microsoft app review. Publisher verification takes minutes once prerequisites are met, but Partner Program account vetting time is not documented.

gates.name: App registration in your own tenant
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own Outlook account through your own Entra app and Composio custom auth config.
limits: Pick a supported account type that works with Composio's /common endpoint; a personal-accounts-only app fails after sign-in
Use the client secret's Value, not its Secret ID

gates.name: User consent / tenant admin consent
gates.unlocks: Users in your tenant, or in tenants whose admins allow it, can consent. By default users can consent to permissions that don't need admin consent. An admin can grant consent for permissions that do.
limits: No test-user allowlist or user cap was found. Access depends on each tenant's consent policy.
Permissions that need admin consent (e.g. Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite) need a tenant admin to approve
Tenants on the microsoft-user-default-low policy only let users consent to verified-publisher apps or apps registered in that tenant, and only for low-impact permissions
Users can still be blocked after admin consent if user consent is restricted in their tenant
Under Microsoft's managed default consent policy, apps that access Exchange/Teams content may need admin approval (reported)
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate in your own tenant. In other tenants it depends on their admin.

gates.name: Publisher verified multitenant app
gates.unlocks: Users in any tenant (and personal accounts, if your account type allows them) can consent without the unverified-app block. Your consent prompt shows the verified badge.
limits: Without verification, users in other tenants can't consent to most new multitenant apps that request more than basic sign-in/profile (when risk-based step-up consent is enabled)
Only possible for apps registered with a work/school account, not a personal Microsoft account
This is a trust signal, not a security certification. Microsoft 365 App Certification is a separate program.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes if you already have a vetted Partner Program PGA account and a verified custom domain. Otherwise depends on Partner Program vetting (not documented).

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app
steps.detail: Composio's managed Outlook app works for prototyping. Switch to your own Entra app if you need any of these: your app name on the consent screen, scopes outside Composio's default set (e.g. Tasks.ReadWrite for To Do), your own rate-limit quota, or trigger polling faster than 15 minutes.

steps.title: Use a work or school Entra account
steps.detail: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with a work or school (Entra ID) account, not a personal Hotmail or Outlook.com account. Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can never be publisher verified, so you would have to re-register later.
gotchas: Consumer accounts get MSANotSupported when they try publisher verification

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Go to Identity > Applications > App registrations > New registration and enter a name. Under Supported account types, choose accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts (AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount). Composio uses the /common endpoint, so this is the safe option. You can leave Redirect URI blank for now.

values.label: Supported account types
values.value: Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts

gotchas: A personal-accounts-only app fails after sign-in with provider_error: invalid_request

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app registration, open Authentication, add a platform of type Web and type the redirect URI in by hand. It must exactly match the redirect URI in your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Some Composio defaults still use the older /api/v1/auth-apps/add callback. Set the same URI explicitly in both Entra and Composio to avoid redirect_uri_mismatch.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and create a client secret
steps.detail: From the app's Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID. Create a client secret and copy its Value straight away; you can't view it again later.
gotchas: Paste the secret's Value, not the Secret ID
Composio's guide suggests a 6- or 12-month expiry. Plan to rotate the secret before it expires.

steps.title: Add the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions
steps.detail: Add the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions your agent will request. Start from Composio's default Outlook set and add extras like Tasks.ReadWrite if you need them. Include offline_access, or you won't get refresh tokens.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: Calendars.Read Calendars.ReadWrite Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared Contacts.ReadWrite Chat.ReadWrite Mail.Read Mail.ReadWrite Mail.Send MailboxSettings.Read MailboxSettings.ReadWrite offline_access User.Read

gotchas: Don't mix /.default with individually listed scopes in the same request

steps.title: Create the Composio custom auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the outlook toolkit with the OAuth2 scheme, turn on own developer credentials, enter the client ID and secret Value, and set the redirect URI. Pass the resulting auth config ID (ac_...) to your sessions.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Test-connect your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through the Connect Link with the new auth config and sign in with your own account. Then confirm a Graph call works, such as listing mail.
gotchas: If sign-in succeeds but the connection fails with invalid_request, check the Supported account types setting

steps.title: Check which scopes need admin consent
steps.detail: Look up each requested permission's AdminConsentRequired flag in Microsoft's Graph permissions reference. Remove any you don't need. For tenants whose admin must approve, prepare a v2.0 adminconsent link built from your client ID, scope list and redirect URI.
gotchas: Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite always needs admin consent. From December 31, 2026 it is required to modify sensitive properties of non-draft messages.

steps.title: Set a publisher domain on a verified custom domain
steps.detail: Add and DNS-verify your own domain in the Entra tenant and set it as the app's publisher domain. A *.onmicrosoft.com publisher domain is not accepted, and the domain must match the email on your Partner Program account.

steps.title: Get a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
steps.detail: Enroll your organization in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program and note the Partner One ID of the partner global account (PGA). Location Partner IDs are not accepted. Associate the PGA with your Entra tenant.
gotchas: MPNAccountNotVetted means the Partner Program account hasn't finished verification yet. You'll have to wait for it.

steps.title: Wait for Partner Program account vetting
steps.detail: Publisher verification can't finish until the Partner Program account is vetted. The findings don't give a timeline for this.

steps.title: Verify the publisher
steps.detail: Sign in with MFA as an Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator who also holds a Partner Admin or Accounts Admin role in Partner Center. Open App registrations > your app > Branding & properties, select Add Partner ID to verify publisher, enter the Partner One ID, accept the developer Terms of Use and save. An agent can do this instead by calling Graph setVerifiedPublisher on the app's object ID.
gotchas: If MFA wasn't done in the same session, verification fails with InteractionRequired
setVerifiedPublisher takes the object ID, not the Application (client) ID

requirements.item: Work or school (Entra ID) account to register the app
requirements.detail: Apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.
Composio uses the common-tenant endpoints. A personal-accounts-only app fails after sign-in.
The Web redirect URI in Entra must exactly match the redirect URI in the Composio auth config.

requirements.item: Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program PGA account
requirements.detail: You need the Partner One ID of the partner global account, associated with your tenant and vetted.
Must not be *.onmicrosoft.com and must match the domain of your Partner Program verification email.

requirements.item: Admin roles and MFA for the person verifying
requirements.detail: Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator in Entra, plus Partner Admin or Accounts Admin in Partner Center. They must sign in with MFA.

requirements.item: Accept the Microsoft identity platform for developers Terms of Use

scopes.effect: Required to get refresh tokens on the v2 endpoint. Without it, connections expire.
Part of Composio's default set. Check its AdminConsentRequired flag in the permissions reference.
Core mail access. The admin-consent flag wasn't captured. Microsoft's managed default consent policy may require admin approval for Exchange content (reported).
Calendar access from the default set. Check the admin-consent flag before shipping.
Contacts access from the default set. Check the admin-consent flag.
Teams chat content. It may fall under the managed consent policy that requires admin approval for Teams content (reported).
The delegated permission doesn't need admin consent. The application version does.
Always needs admin consent. Required from December 31, 2026 to modify sensitive properties of non-draft messages.
Not in Composio's managed set, so To Do tools return 401 there. You need a custom auth config to add it.

blockers.symptom: Connection fails after sign-in with provider_error: invalid_request
blockers.cause: The app is registered for personal Microsoft accounts only, but Composio uses the /common endpoint.
blockers.fix: Change Supported account types (manifest signInAudience) to AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount.

blockers.cause: The Entra redirect URI doesn't exactly match Composio's, for example because an old v1 callback is still set as a default.
blockers.fix: Set the same Composio callback URL explicitly in both the Entra Authentication page and the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Users in other organisations can't consent to the app
blockers.cause: Risk-based step-up consent blocks most new multitenant apps that aren't publisher verified and request more than basic sign-in/profile.
blockers.fix: Complete publisher verification, or have each tenant's admin grant consent.

blockers.symptom: Standard users still see 'approval required' after admin consent
blockers.cause: User consent is disabled or restricted in their tenant.
blockers.fix: Their admin should check Enterprise applications > Consent and permissions > User consent settings, or turn on the admin consent workflow.

blockers.symptom: Publisher verification errors MPNGlobalAccountNotFound, MPNAccountNotVetted or PublisherDomainMismatch
blockers.cause: A location Partner ID was used, the Partner Program account isn't vetted yet, or the publisher domain doesn't match the Partner Program email domain.
blockers.fix: Use the PGA Partner One ID, wait for vetting, and align the publisher domain with a DNS-verified domain that matches the Partner Program email.

blockers.cause: A consumer Microsoft account was used.
blockers.fix: Register and verify the app with a work or school Entra account.

blockers.cause: MFA wasn't performed in the same session, or the user is flagged as risky.
blockers.fix: Sign in again with MFA. For UnableToAddPublisher, Microsoft suggests retrying the next day.

blockers.cause: The app is in a national-cloud tenant.
blockers.fix: Register the app in a commercial-cloud tenant.

blockers.symptom: To Do tools return 401 on managed auth
blockers.cause: Composio's managed Outlook app doesn't include Tasks scopes.
blockers.fix: Use a custom auth config with Tasks.ReadWrite added.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Outlook app to build and prototype. Users will see a Composio-branded consent screen, quota is shared, and trigger polling is limited to 15 minutes. Move to your own Entra app when you need your own branding, extra scopes such as Tasks.ReadWrite (missing from the managed set), your own quota, or faster polling. Register the app for organizational and personal accounts, because Composio uses /common. Paste the client secret's Value and Composio's exact callback URL.
